subject.title: [Bug]: clearUnboundScopes strips operator scopes unconditionally for non-local token-auth clients

question: Should OpenClaw support device-less shared-token/password WebSocket operators by granting configured scopes, or continue requiring device identity/device tokens for remote write-capable clients?
rationale: The source-reproducible failure is real, but the repair decides whether possession of the shared Gateway token can grant operator.write or stronger scopes without device identity, which is a Gateway auth boundary decision automation should not make alone.

options.title: Land Bounded Token Scopes
options.body: Approve and land a bounded tokenScopes-style policy with non-loopback privileged-scope safeguards, docs, upgrade proof, and real Gateway behavior proof.

options.title: Require Device Identity
options.body: Keep remote device-less shared-token clients scope-empty and close or retarget linked work to document device-token/pairing requirements for write-capable clients.

options.title: Defer Auth Direction
options.body: Leave this and the tokenScopes design open until Gateway/security owners choose the trust model for headless deployments.

recommendation.title: Land Bounded Token Scopes
recommendation.body: Approve and land a bounded tokenScopes-style policy with non-loopback privileged-scope safeguards, docs, upgrade proof, and real Gateway behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the current tokenScopes proposal owner and a recent contributor to the Gateway auth/config surface that would carry the decision.
